correctness.rationale: Let g=|γ|² and r1,r2=(4+αβ+g∓Δ)/(2√2β), Δ²=(αβ+g−4)²+16g. Squaring a putative crossing rj=1 and subtracting Δ² produces exactly −4√2β(αβ−2√2α−√2β+g+4). For β≠2√2 this gives αc=(2β−√2(g+4))/(√2β−4). Sign of the signed radical selects r1 for β<2√2, r2 for β>2√2; derivative at crossing is (1/√2)(β−2√2)²/[(β−2√2)²+2g]>0. Independently simplified original αhat−αc=7g/[2β(√2β−4)]. Numerical substitution (β,g)=(1,1) gives αc≈1.961131723051 with r1=1; at β=2√2 g>0 crossing equation impossible. g=0 singular line treated separately. Calculations are identities over the stated parameter domain; examples alone would not prove it.
